typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source slide 9 / page.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source slide 9 / page.

recognitionRules: Use comic-style illustration with clear, flat reading panels.
Keep the token budget in a distinct high-contrast block.
Use Trebuchet for rules and large numbered stages.
Make the team goal and option costs explicit before play.
Keep think, speak or write participation routes available.

principles: Use short action sentences; follow an invitation with a concrete material, choice or check.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: One team. Two ideas. Six tokens. What will you make possible?
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid promises that every participant will master the skill.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: Try one version, then compare it with the criterion.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use THE POP-UP PLAN in Trebuchet with two offset open rectangles and one small token circle. Avoid a trophy or competitive victory mark.
invariants: Use comic-style illustration with clear, flat reading panels.
Keep the token budget in a distinct high-contrast block.
Use Trebuchet for rules and large numbered stages.
adaptations: A facilitator sheet prioritizes rules and costs over illustration.
A participant card keeps the current round and budget visible.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.
